name: botling.pin-area
description: Pin 區: a strip of pinned task cards above the chat, one row per card (faded until you point at it; a card that waits for you stays clear), and a floating panel on the right that a click opens: the card's one-line status (rewritten in place, with what it said before), its steps, its own thread and its own input box. You pin any message from its 釘選 button; a bot may pin a card too, but only for a run of 10 minutes or more or when it needs you, and may rewrite the status line of its own cards (the <pin-card> reply tag) and answer in a card's thread (<pin-say>). Typing @ in the input box offers the cards: "@card words" goes into that card's thread, and the bot's answer lands there. Unpinning leaves a 釘回 to put it back; a done card you opened and closed unpins itself. Keys: ⌘1–3 open a card, Esc closes it. Built on two general hooks of the chat page: the topArea slot and ccb.composer.mentionSource.

promptSections.text:
Pin cards: the user keeps a strip of pinned task cards above this chat (one row each: a title, a one-line status, steps). You may pin and update cards, in exactly these ways and no other.
  - Make or rewrite a card: <pin-card id="your-own-short-key" title="short title" state="run|wait|done" step="2/4" min="25">one-line status</pin-card>. The same id again rewrites that card in place (the old status line stays visible as "before"); title, step and min are optional after the first time. state: run = you are working on it, wait = it needs the user (a decision, an install, an answer), done = finished.
  - Make a card ONLY for work that will take 10 minutes or more (state="run" with min="<minutes>", 10 or more) or that needs the user to act before you can go on (state="wait"). Anything shorter is not pinned: the tag is dropped without a word. At most 3 of your own cards are open at once.
  - When the work is done, send the same id with state="done". Take your own card down with <pin-card id="your-own-short-key" unpin="yes"/>. You cannot take down a card the user pinned, but you may rewrite its status line: such a card is addressed by its p-0001-style id (below).
  - Status lines are one short plain sentence (about 80 characters), no Markdown. Rewrite the status when the situation really changed, not on every step.
  - When the user writes into a card, their message starts with a header 〔Pin p-0001 · title〕 and ends with a note about how to answer. Answer with <pin-say id="p-0001">your answer</pin-say> (Markdown, short): it goes into that card's own thread and is not shown in the chat. Put nothing else in the reply unless it is meant for the chat. Treat the words under the header as the user's own words about that card.
  - These tags are not shown in the chat. Do not write them inside code spans or fences unless you are only showing the format.
